published_statement: Sec. 7 (Discussion, p.30): 'While the latter [shape functions or embedding diagrams] can certainly be used without risk for detecting flare-out in static wormholes, they are at best misleading if applied to dynamic wormholes. This is simply because the embedding of a wormhole spacetime requires selecting and lifting out a particular time-slice and embedding this instantaneous spatial three-geometry in a flat Euclidean R3. For a static wormhole, any constant time-slice will suffice, and if the embedded surface is flared-out in the spatial direction orthogonal to the throat, then it is flared-out in spacetime as well. But if the wormhole is dynamic, flare-out in the spatial direction does not imply flare-out in the null directions orthogonal to the throat.' Sec. 4 (p.11): '...suggests why it is that the embedding of the spatial part of a wormhole spacetime in an Euclidean R3 is no longer a reliable operational technique for defining "flare-out" in the time-dependent case.' Definition 4.1.1 (p.14): 'A two-surface satisfies the "simple flare-out" condition iff it is extremal, theta = 0, and also satisfies dtheta/du >= 0' (= marginally anti-trapped surface). Sec. 5.1 eq. (49)-(50) (p.19): at a throat, dtheta/du + sigma_ab sigma^ab = -8 pi T_ab l^a l^b, so simple flare-out gives T_ab l^a l^b <= 0: 'The NEC is therefore either violated, or on the verge of being violated'; strong flare-out (eq. 51) gives strict violation at some point; strongly anti-trapped (eq. 52) everywhere; averaged flare-out gives the sign-averaged NEC violation over the throat (eq. 53). Near the throat (p.21): NEC 'violating, or on the verge of violating' along partial null curves {x} x (0, u*_x). Sec. 6.1 eq. (77) and 6.2 eq. (90): in the two worked examples, a null throat is simply flared iff the NEC is violated or on the verge there; 'temporary suspension of the violation of the NEC at a time-dependent throat also leads to a simultaneous obliteration of the flare-out property of the throat itself' (p.30).
published_hypotheses: H1 DEFINITIONAL: a throat is a closed, two-sided, spacelike 2-surface on which the expansion of ONE future-directed orthogonal null congruence vanishes (theta_+ = 0 or theta_- = 0) and whose derivative along that same null direction is >= 0 (simple), >0 somewhere (strong), >0 everywhere (strongly anti-trapped), sign-averaged >0 (averaged), or N-fold degenerate (Defs 4.1.1-4.1.6, Table 1). Flare-out is defined on NULL congruences, 'free from notions of embedding and shape-functions'

H2 Einstein equation G_ab = 8 pi T_ab (eq. 11), optionally plus a totally antisymmetric (Kalb-Ramond) torsion H = dA (Sec. 2, 5.2); the NEC statements are about the total T_ab contracted with the SAME null congruence that defines the throat (p.19)
H3 no symmetry, no asymptotic flatness, no topology, no staticity assumed (abstract, p.3); the congruences are surface-orthogonal hence twist-free (eq. 55-57)
H4 smoothness: Taylor expansion of theta in affine parameter near the throat (eq. 38), used for the near-throat statements (eq. 59); degenerate throats handled by eq. (39)-(41)
H5 the NEC conclusion under SIMPLE flare-out is NON-STRICT: T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 ('violated, or on the verge of being violated'); strict violation needs strong flare-out
H6 the conclusion is the NEC (a null contraction of T_ab), not the WEC, not negative energy density, not negative Misner-Sharp mass

H7 the Sec. 7 sentence is a NON-IMPLICATION remark in the Discussion, not a numbered theorem; its support in the paper is the Sec. 4 variational argument (dynamic throats need independent null deformations delta u_+, delta u_-), the Sec. 4.2 static-coalescence proof (eqs. 43-48, Killing-adapted constant-t slice), and the Sec. 6.1 worked example (conformally rescaled Morris-Thorne, eq. 69) where the spatial 'center' r0 differs from the null throats r*(t) and 'the center of the wormhole is the wrong place to look for NEC violations, except in the static limit' (Sec. 6.1.4)
H8 'static' in the Sec. 7 equivalence means the constant-Killing-time slice (eq. 43: V^a = e^phi (d/dt)^a orthogonal to the slices)

DROPPED (class of objects: null throats) driven.py:311-312 and driven.py:516-518 (standard_table REFUTED row 'therefore the corridor needs no negative energy' -- 'Hochberg & Visser 1998; Olum 1998'), driven.py:493-494 (PRIOR_ART_REFUTATION) and driven.py:84 ('the consequence, read as an escape, was refuted in print in 1998'). HV 9802046 refutes a specific move: temporarily suspending NEC violation at a dynamic wormhole while keeping a NULL-flared throat (their refs [21-25]; eqs. 77, 90). Its theorems reach a spherically contracting corridor only if the corridor contains a marginally anti-trapped surface with null flare-out (H1). HV's own Sec. 7 says a spatial (slice) criterion -- which Gamma > 1 is, driven.py:89 'THIS FILE'S CRITERION IS A CONSTANT-t SPATIAL CRITERION' -- does not imply null flare-out. So HV cannot, by itself, carry 'needs negative energy' for a spatially defined corridor. Maeda-Harada-Carr 0901.1153 (read) exhibit dynamic throats that are minimal spheres on spacelike slices and satisfy the DEC everywhere (re-derived here: MHC eq. 4.53, a = t/t0, radial NEC at the throat iff t0 <= b). The REFUTED row also cites Olum 1998, which the tree itself calls 'the one that governs the project' (driven.py:103-108). Whether the row stands on Olum alone is a separate audit (gr-qc/9805003), not decided here.

DROPPED (energy condition named) driven.py:311-312, 516-518: 'needs no negative energy'. HV's conclusion is an NEC statement, T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 (H6), not negative energy density (WEC) and not m < 0. NEC violation does not by itself imply negative energy density for any observer.

All computed from the metric with a hand-rolled Christoffel/Ricci/Einstein routine and theta = gamma^{ab} nabla_a l_b (HV eq. 16 projector), not from HV's printed formulas. AGREE: eq. (15) normalisation of (71); (72) theta_+-; (73) dtheta_+-/du_+-; (74) throat condition; (75) flare-out on theta = 0; (76) G_tt^ + G_rr^; (77) on theta = 0, dtheta/du = -(G_tt^+G_rr^)/2 = -4 pi (rho - tau), so NEC holds iff not flared; Raychaudhuri with sigma = omega = 0 including the non-affinity term kappa theta (HV p.11 technical aside); static coalescence theta_+ = -theta_- (Sec. 4.2/6.1.3); (85) normalisation; (87) theta_-; (88) flare-out at 2m = r; (90) sign equivalence. SEC. 7 COUNTEREXAMPLE, CONSTRUCTED AND CHECKED: in HV's own family (69) with b = r0^2/r (r0 = 1) and Omega = exp(t/4 - 5t^2/2), the t = 0 slice flares out spatially at r0 (d2A/ds2 = 1 > 0, b'(r0) = -1 < 1); the spatial throat r0 has theta_+ = sqrt2/4 != 0, so it is not null-extremal; the only null-extremal spheres of patch 1 at t = 0 (r* = 1.0352761804, 3.8637033052) both have dtheta_-/du_- < 0 (-4.1919872981, -5.0580127019, equal to HV (75) in closed form); so the slice is spatially flared but no round sphere at t = 0 is a null-flared throat, and the NEC holds there, as (77) requires. Control k = 0 (no deceleration): the inner r* IS null-flared (+0.8080127019), so the failure is caused by Omega-ddot and the example is not rigged. DISCREPANCIES, text layer (sign-preserving, none load-bearing): (83) prints (1/r0^2)(1 - b'(r0)); computed (1 - b'(r0))/(2 r0^2), consistent with HV's own (73) at Omega = 1. (86) prints theta_+ = (1/2) e^psi (1 - 2m/r); computed e^psi (1 - 2m/r)/r; HV's own (88) follows only from the corrected form. (89) prints dm/dv = 4 pi r^2 T_vv; computed 4 pi r^2 e^{-psi} T_vv (e^{-psi} > 0). (47) prints l-+ = (1/2)(V +- n), which gives l+.l- = -1/2, violating (15); 1/sqrt2 is required. Sec. 6.1.1 'there is therefore, always only one extremal hypersurface in the first patch': true as 'only one of theta_+, theta_-', but for b = r0^2/r and 0 < h < 1/(2 r0), eq. (74) has TWO roots in r, which the script exhibits. Wording, not a refutation: at both roots the flare-out formula (75) and the equivalence (77) hold. LATER-LITERATURE CHECK: Maeda-Harada-Carr (4.58)-(4.59) re-derived. At their spatial throat x = 0, 8 pi (mu + p_r) = 2(1 - t0^2/b^2)/t^2 >= 0 iff t0 <= b. x = 0 is a minimal sphere of the t = const slice and is trapped (theta_+ = theta_- = sqrt2/t), i.e. spatially flared, not null-flared, and NEC-satisfying.

later_literature.what: HV-type and Hayward-type throats (minimal spheres on NULL hypersurfaces) must violate the NEC (their eq. 3.8 re-derives HV's result: d_+ theta_+ = -8 pi G T_++ on theta_+ = 0). But 'these definitions are not well-motivated in a cosmological background' and 'miss an important class of dynamical wormhole spacetimes'. With a throat defined as a minimal sphere on a SPACELIKE hypersurface, a dynamic throat can be a trapped sphere and 'there may be no violation of the energy conditions'. Analytic example: conformal Ellis, a = t/t0, DEC holds everywhere for t0 <= b. This confirms HV's Sec. 7 non-implication from the other side, and shows that the NEC conclusion rests on the null-throat definition (H1).

later_literature.what: Independently reaches HV's conclusion that negative energy (NEC violation) is required generically, via temporal outer trapping horizons, with the NEC violated everywhere on a generic wormhole horizon. Criticises HV's definition: 'Hochberg & Visser specifically allow spatial horizons, in which case their flare-out condition selects maximal rather than minimal surfaces in a time-symmetric hypersurface', and HV's non-strict flare-out admits degenerate cases in which 'negative energy could just barely be avoided in very special cases' (unstable, 'useless for practical transport'). Consistent with H5: non-strict flare-out gives only 'violated or on the verge'.

Surfaced; titles and abstracts concern dynamical and evolving wormholes built on Morris-Thorne/Ellis with time dependence. None was read beyond the abstract. No refutation of HV's Sec. 5 theorems or Sec. 7 remark appeared in the sweep.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: there is no datum to lack. HV 9802046 is a mathematical statement in classical GR -- the Raychaudhuri equation, the Einstein equation and a definition of throat. The Sec. 7 remark is a non-implication, which one counterexample settles, and the script builds one in HV's own metric family. No constant, measurement or extrapolation enters, so no later data can move the conclusion (evidence: the full text contains no numerical input; data_at_publication records none). What DID come later is definitional, not observational. (a) Maeda-Harada-Carr 2009 showed that the NEC conclusion depends on defining the throat on NULL hypersurfaces: spatially defined dynamic throats can satisfy the DEC. (b) Hayward 1999 showed that HV's non-strict flare-out admits degenerate cases where the NEC is only 'on the verge'. Neither contradicts HV. Both mark the edge of HV's class, and that edge is where the tree's REFUTED row over-reaches. The Sec. 7 remark STANDS against everything read. The text-layer discrepancies (83), (86), (89), (47) are misprints or extraction artefacts, recorded as discrepancies, and none changes a sign or a conclusion.
grade_evidence: The statement the tree quotes -- Sec. 7, 'if the wormhole is dynamic, flare-out in the spatial direction does not imply flare-out in the null directions orthogonal to the throat', and the Sec. 4 embedding remark -- is READ verbatim at source and would grade STANDS on its own. It is re-derived with an explicit sympy counterexample in HV's family (69), HV's (72)-(77) and (88), (90) are recomputed from the metric and agree, and Maeda-Harada-Carr 2009 confirm it. The grade is NARROWED because the tree rests more on this key than the source carries. (1) driven.standard_table's REFUTED row 'therefore the corridor needs no negative energy', PRIOR_ART_REFUTATION and driven.py:84 'refuted in print in 1998' extend HV's NEC theorems to a spatially defined corridor. HV's theorems apply only at null-flared marginally anti-trapped surfaces (H1), and HV's own Sec. 7 is the reason a slice criterion does not reach them. MHC's DEC-satisfying dynamic spatial throat, re-derived here, shows the gap is real. (2) HV conclude an NEC statement, non-strict under simple flare-out (H5, H6); the tree's row speaks of 'negative energy'. (3) foliation.py:616 'REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE -- Hochberg & Visser 1998' drops the strict/non-strict distinction. Guarding against over-representation both ways: this is not WRONG for any tree line. The row's verdict may still stand on Olum 1998, which it also cites and which the tree itself calls governing; that is audited under gr-qc/9805003, not here. The HV misprints are discrepancies, not refutations.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: if the tree's REFUTED row and PRIOR_ART_REFUTATION were re-scoped to cite HV only for null-flared throats ('suspending the NEC at a dynamic throat destroys the throat') and carried the non-strict 'violated or on the verge' qualifier, leaving the corridor's energy requirement to Olum (gr-qc/9805003). Alternatively, if the corridor in driven.py/nonstatic.py were shown to contain a marginally anti-trapped sphere with null flare-out. HV's theorem would then apply to it directly (T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 there). To WRONG: only a counterexample to HV's Sec. 5 theorem itself, which is ruled out by the Raychaudhuri identity recomputed in the script, or a computation showing the Sec. 7 non-implication false, which the explicit counterexample rules out. To OPEN: none. The source is read in full and every checkable claim was checked.
